# Report: order-290-readiness-case-pylavi

Status: complete (report only). Two pinned public VIs have explicit saved-property expectations independent of inspecting their bytes; #169 readiness remains unmet.
The proposed case below covers saved version, separate compiled code and debugging, with opposite flag expectations to distinguish constant answers.
Evidence: `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT/pylavi/tests/test.yaml` lines 86–125 and `pylavi/validate.py` lines 402–415, 460–466; source hashes are embedded below.
`args.yaml` lines 23–29 corroborates version 21.0f for test VIs; its `path_length: 128` is a maximum filesystem-path length, not a native VI property (`validate.py:566–568`).
The actual debugging key is `not_debuggable`, not `no_debugging`; `breakpoints: false` disables that check and does not assert breakpoint presence (`validate.py:571–576`).
Controlled input → output expectation: **none found in the bounded search**. The four matches concerned assembler arguments and an add.vi breakpoint test, not numeric execution expectations.
Search covered 35 Python/YAML/Markdown files under pylavi, files ≤200,000 bytes, with a 60-match cap; pattern: `add\.vi|expected[_ ]?(output|result)|CallByReference|call_by_reference|input.*output|output.*input` (case insensitive).
Earlier alias Greps returned no matches; `rg` was unavailable, so bounded Python text searches supplied interpreting-code discovery and the substantive I/O search. No VI bytes were interpreted; hashing used `python3 -I`.
Verification: `python3 -I -B benchmark/scripts/native_jobs.py --check` exited 0: “Native design valid: 23/23 slots mapped; 12 recipes; zero native executions. Known-behaviour readiness prerequisite unresolved.”
No native execution happened. No repository files were changed, no standalone case was installed, and no commit was run; only this session report was written.
